title: First Amendment — speech & assembly (educational summary)
excerpt: Educational summary: the First Amendment limits Congress from restricting free speech, peaceful assembly, petition, and the free exercise of religion. Courts balance these rights against time/place/manner rules and narrow categories (e.g. true threats). Always check current Supreme Court doctrine and federal vs state application.

title: Fourth Amendment — searches & seizures (educational summary)
excerpt: Educational summary: the Fourth Amendment protects people from unreasonable searches and seizures and generally requires a warrant supported by probable cause, with many exceptions developed by courts (consent, exigent circumstances, automobile rules, etc.).

title: Fifth Amendment — due process & self-incrimination (educational summary)
excerpt: Educational summary: the Fifth Amendment includes grand jury indictment (with exceptions), double jeopardy protections, due process of law, and the privilege against compelled self-incrimination in criminal cases. Civil and administrative contexts have different rules.

title: Fourteenth Amendment — equal protection (educational summary)
excerpt: Educational summary: the Fourteenth Amendment extends federal due process and equal protection constraints to the states and underpins much modern civil-rights law. Courts apply varying levels of scrutiny depending on the classification or right involved.

title: Article II — executive power (educational summary)
excerpt: Educational summary: Article II vests executive power in the President, including commander-in-chief authority, appointment powers (with Senate advice and consent for principal officers), and a duty to faithfully execute the laws—subject to separation-of-powers limits enforced by Congress and courts.
